CATE via DNN rank-weighted pseudo-outcome averaging

Source: R/user-dnn-cate.R
cate_dnn.Rd

Estimate conditional average treatment effects by combining a pseudo-outcome with DNN-based local weights.

Usage

cate_dnn(
  data = NULL,
  x_cols = NULL,
  y_col = NULL,
  t_col = NULL,
  m0_col = NULL,
  m1_col = NULL,
  m_col = NULL,
  e_col = NULL,
  pseudo_outcome = NULL,
  X = NULL,
  X0 = NULL,
  x0 = NULL,
  clip = 1e-08,
  distance = "l2",
  method = c("exact", "asymp"),
  k = 1L,
  s = NULL,
  tuning = NULL,
  tuning_mode = c("default", "grid"),
  normalize = TRUE,
  se = TRUE,
  jackknife = c("fast", "loo", "none"),
  ctx = NULL,
  return = c("W")
)

Arguments

data

Data frame with covariates and optional nuisance columns. Column names must be non-missing, non-empty, and unique.

x_cols

Names or indices of covariate columns in data.

y_col

Name or index of the outcome column in data.

t_col

Name or index of the treatment column in data (must be 0/1).

m0_col

Name or index for \(E[Y(0)\mid X]\) (full AIPW interface).

m1_col

Name or index for \(E[Y(1)\mid X]\) (full AIPW interface).

m_col

Name or index for \(E[Y\mid X]\) (Robinson interface).

e_col

Name or index for propensity \(P(T=1\mid X)\).

pseudo_outcome

Numeric vector of length n. If supplied, nuisance columns are not required.

X

Numeric matrix (n x p) for the matrix interface.

X0

Numeric matrix (m x p) of target points; mutually exclusive with x0.

x0

Numeric vector of length p for a single target point.

clip

Finite propensity clipping constant in (0, 0.5) with 1 - clip < 1 in double precision, default 1e-8. Raw nuisance propensities must be finite and lie in [0, 1]; nuisance-based AIPW and Robinson scores use pmin(pmax(e, clip), 1 - clip). This argument does not alter a supplied pseudo_outcome.

distance

Distance name or specification (for example "l2").

method

One of "exact" or "asymp" for DNN weights.

k

Integer DNN neighbour count inside each size-s subsample. The paper theory uses k = 1 (the default).

s

Integer kernel order (undersmoothing parameter), or NULL. When both s and tuning are NULL (the default), s is resolved from the paper undersmoothing rule tuning_dnn_paper(), \(s = \lfloor 0.4 n^{(k_x+1)/(k_x+2)} \rfloor\). Note that small fixed values such as s = 1 (or k = s) yield uniform weights and hence no localization; a warning is emitted in that case.

tuning

Optional kernel-order tuning specification. When supplied, s must be omitted and is resolved from tuning.

tuning_mode

One of "default" or "grid". "default" evaluates the default s only. "grid" evaluates the feasible candidates from tuning, or from tuning_dnn_paper() when tuning is omitted, and stores candidate-level estimates, standard errors, diagnostics, and metadata in tuning_grid. Grid mode cannot be combined with explicit s.

normalize

Logical; renormalize columns of W to sum to 1.

se

Logical; compute delete-1 jackknife standard errors.

jackknife

One of "fast", "loo", or "none". "fast" (default) uses cached full-sample ranks with delete-1 rank updates, "loo" recomputes leave-one-out weights directly, and "none" skips SEs.

ctx

Optional context passed to distance and ranking components.

return

Optional extras in addition to the always-returned tau, se, and meta. Allowed values: c("W", "ranks", "ord", "dx", "psi", "nuisance", "ess", "neighbors", "tuning"). The neighbors extra returns the first k nearest observations used inside each size-s subsample, not the full DNN weight support.

Value

An object of class cate_result with components:

  • tau: estimated CATE values at target points;

  • se: optional jackknife standard errors;

  • x0: the m x p matrix of evaluation points, with covariate column names propagated from the training data when available;

  • meta: metadata (n, m, p, k, s, method, distance);

  • tuning_grid: in grid mode, a list with candidates, estimates, diagnostics, and meta tables. Candidate diagnostics report top-5 weight concentration separately from the estimator's k;

  • optional extras requested via return.

Details

Two interfaces are supported.

  1. Data-frame interface (recommended): pass data and x_cols, then provide either pseudo_outcome directly or nuisance columns used to construct it. For nuisance columns, use either:

    • full AIPW form: y_col, t_col, e_col, m0_col, m1_col;

    • Robinson form: y_col, t_col, e_col, m_col.

  2. Matrix interface: pass X, one of X0 or x0, and pseudo_outcome.

As in weights_dnn(), exact DNN localization uses the full rank permutation at each target rather than an s-nearest-neighbor truncation. The "fast" jackknife option reuses the full-sample rank matrix and updates ranks under deletion. For exact DNN fits, the finite-population support edge is rank n - s + k, not rank s.

tuning_mode = "default" evaluates only the default kernel order and preserves the ordinary scalar-fit return shape. tuning_mode = "grid" evaluates the feasible candidates in tuning, or the paper default tuning grid when tuning is omitted, and attaches a tidy tuning_grid payload. The pseudo-outcome and nuisance columns are resolved once before grid evaluation. The primary tau, se, meta, and optional extras such as W, ranks, ess, psi, and nuisance remain anchored to the default candidate. Full per-candidate weight matrices are not stored. Candidate diagnostics include ess, max_weight, top_n, top5_weight_share, and degenerate; top_n is fixed at 5 and is independent of the estimator's k.

The AIPW signal is Neyman orthogonal at the true nuisance functions. The normalized Robinson signal identifies the effect with true nuisances but is generally not orthogonal to propensity error. If the pooled outcome mean is correct, its conditional expectation is \(e_0(1-e_0)\tau / \{\hat e(1-\hat e)\}\). It can therefore have first-order propensity drift; AIPW's orthogonality argument does not apply to that route without additional propensity control. Orthogonality alone does not validate arbitrary nuisance predictions fitted on the same observations used for localization and inference. Valid full-sample reuse additionally requires the nuisance-rate and full-state stability conditions in the accompanying paper. This function computes the estimator and its requested jackknife procedure; it cannot diagnose whether an arbitrary learner satisfies those conditions. Supply oracle quantities, cross-fitted or out-of-fold predictions, or full-sample predictions from a learner for which the paper's rate and stability conditions are credible.

With data, omit X; a direct pseudo_outcome vector remains supported. Column selectors require data. Prediction retains the fitted metric and context even if a registered distance name is subsequently replaced.

See also

weights_dnn(), weights_matrix(), score_cate_rho(), cate_demo_data().

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 50
x_mat <- matrix(rnorm(n * 2), n, 2)
x0_mat <- matrix(rnorm(6), 3, 2)
psi <- rnorm(n)
out <- cate_dnn(
  X = x_mat, X0 = x0_mat, pseudo_outcome = psi,
  distance = "l2", method = "exact", k = 1L, s = 3L,
  se = FALSE, return = c("W", "ess")
)
out$tau
#> [1] -0.02293282 -0.04260484 -0.24413829
